Posterior summary of the factor-implied shared variation matrix

Source: R/shared_variation.R
shared_variation.Rd

For a latent-factor mvgam fit, returns the posterior of the shared variation matrix \(\Delta = Z \Sigma Z^\top\). Z is the n_series x n_lv loadings matrix and \(\Sigma\) is the covariance of the latent states. Delta is the covariance the factors induce between the series' trends. Its diagonal gives the variance of each series that the factors capture. Its off-diagonal entries give the covariance between pairs of series.

Usage

shared_variation(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
shared_variation(object, probs = c(0.025, 0.975), robust = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted mvgam object whose trend model includes latent factors (n_lv < n_series).

...

Unused. Anything passed here is refused.

probs

Two probabilities for the lower and upper bounds of the credible interval. Default c(0.025, 0.975), a 95% interval.

robust

Logical. If FALSE (the default), uses mean and standard deviation for summaries. If TRUE, uses median and median absolute deviation (MAD).

Value

An object of class mvgam_shared_variation, a list with:

  • delta: posterior point estimate of the n_series x n_series shared variation matrix.

  • delta_se: posterior spread per entry.

  • delta_lower, delta_upper: per-entry credible bounds at probs.

  • delta_ess: per-entry effective sample size, from posterior::ess_basic().

  • n_series, series_names, n_lv: model dimensions and series labels.

  • probs, robust: the summary settings.

Details

A factor column enters the trend as sigma_trend[k] * Z[, k]. Z Z' alone would weight every column equally, while the model scales each column by its latent standard deviation. Under multiplicative gamma process shrinkage those scales hold the whole of the shrinkage. For an autoregressive trend \(\Sigma\) is the stationary covariance of the latent states, as in residual_cor().

Delta is invariant to rotation. An orthogonal Z* = Z Q with Sigma* = Q' Sigma Q leaves Z* Sigma* Z*' unchanged. The summary takes the same value for the sampled Z and for the QR-identified Z_tilde of Heaps and Jermyn (2024). It uses the sampled Z, the basis \(\Sigma\) is stated in. A trend_map without NA entries fixes Z. The posterior spread of Delta then comes from \(\Sigma\) alone.

Relation to loadings_prior

Under the matrix-normal prior Z | Phi, Psi ~ MN(0, Phi, Psi), the prior expectation of Z Z' is tr(Psi) Phi (Heaps and Jermyn 2024, section 3). Phi sets the prior expectation of the coupling pattern between series, while Z itself is identified only up to rotation. A loadings_prior in mvgam() encodes domain knowledge about that pattern through Phi.

Delta also carries the latent covariance. Its scale includes the variance of the latent states. Compare its pattern with Phi.

References

Heaps, S. E. and Jermyn, I. H. (2024). Structured prior distributions for the covariance matrix in latent factor models. Statistics and Computing, 34:143. doi:10.1007/s11222-024-10454-0

See also

residual_cor() for the implied correlation matrix, cov2cor(Delta). Under mvn() and mvt() it adds each series' residual variance to the diagonal of Delta first. The joint species distribution article interprets both for a community of species.

Other latent dynamics: active_factors(), compare_loadings(), fevd.mvgam(), irf.mvgam(), ordinate(), posterior_transition_matrix(), residual_cor(), stability.mvgam()

Examples

# \dontrun{
# Detections of 6 species whose occupancy shares two latent factors
simdat <- sim_closure_unit_data(
  family    = occ(),
  n_species = 6L,
  n_sites   = 80L,
  n_visits  = 4L,
  n_lv      = 2L,
  seed      = 1L
)
mod <- jsdgam(
  formula        = bf(y ~ series * env, p ~ series + tod_c),
  factor_formula = ~ -1,
  data           = simdat$data_train,
  family         = occ(),
  n_lv           = 2L,
  chains         = 2,
  silent         = 2
)
#> Warning: 49 of 2000 (2.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

# The species-by-species covariance the two factors induce
sv <- shared_variation(mod)
sv
#> Factor-implied shared variation matrix (Delta = Z Sigma Z')
#>   6 series x 2 latent factors | point = posterior mean, spread = SD
#>   Quantile bounds: [0.025, 0.975] 
#> 
#> Diagonal (captured variance per series):
#>      Estimate  Q2.5  Q97.5
#> sp_1    3.181 0.014 35.988
#> sp_2    2.668 0.037 20.761
#> sp_3    2.014 0.013 16.764
#> sp_4    1.267 0.015  7.893
#> sp_5    6.781 0.036 63.237
#> sp_6    1.807 0.017  9.492
#> 
#> plot() draws the full matrix as a heatmap.
plot(sv)
